A relatively small number of hydrotests have been conducted at upper and lower stockpile-to-target sequence temperatures (in a long soak configuration). Actual environments may deviate signifi- cantly from these conditions. Complex environments, beyond static thermal tests, can include dynamic thermal events, static or dynamic g-loading, and/or hostile environments. The ability to simulate, mock-up, or recreate more complex environments during a hydrodynamic test enables weapon designers to study what these effects would have on performance, safety, and surety. Hydrodynamic testing at DARHT can also be done on samples previously exposed to hostile conditions, to study the effects of hostile environments on outcomes. Studying hydrodynamics under these conditions also limits the chance for technology surprise. Given the inherent 3D nature of these prob- lems, additional viewing axes at DARHT are highly desirable to maximize the understanding and analysis of these effects. Three-dimensional experimental results will support validation of current modeling and help to advance 2D modeling to 3D modeling. It should be noted that additional viewing axes are also highly desirable for global secu- rity, safety, and surety scenarios independent of complex environments.
